quote: That that the the Tesla panels, they that's something only Tesla does. We're a certified Tesla arm installer, but only for their batteries.
stewart_read: Rep partially corrects the Tesla misconception (batteries only) but never mentions Ion's own panel line, missing the chance to redirect interest toward what Ion actually sells.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could have been intentionally simplifying to avoid confusing a lead he was about to DQ — but the same clarification opportunity existed before the DQ decision was made.
coaching_implication: When correcting a Tesla product misconception, always pivot to 'here's what we do install' per context.tesla_relationship_clarification's correct_framing_for_setter.

quote: I I'm taking a look, and it looks like you have too much shade for us to make our system work anyway. So I'll just get back to us for now.
stewart_read: Rep disqualifies without any confirming question to the customer (e.g., asking about tree removal plans) and without a locked next step — the DQ is stated as fact from rep's own satellite look rather than explored with the customer.
alternative_hypothesis: Shade may be a genuinely hard, unrecoverable gate the rep correctly identified early to save both parties time.
coaching_implication: Before DQing on shade, ask if trees are being trimmed/removed — an easy enthusiasm-signal check that was skipped here.

quote: I've said before, if they build racks in the back part of my yard, that would solve the problem.
stewart_read: Customer directly offers a workaround (ground racks in the yard) that could resolve the shade DQ, but rep had already closed the roof-mount-only door moments earlier.
coaching_implication: Customer proposing his own solution is a strong buying signal; rep should have paused the DQ to explore ground-mount feasibility before fully closing the door.

quote: what do you know about the Tesla panels? I mean, you know, they look like just the size of a big TV or something. And I don't know. Is that enough to power a house?
stewart_read: Rep answers a detailed technical/product-capacity question about a product Ion doesn't even sell, well past the point of any appointment or sale being possible.
alternative_hypothesis: Since the lead is already DQ'd, this could be seen as harmless customer-service chat rather than true scope creep with sales stakes.
coaching_implication: Once DQ'd, redirect quickly rather than getting pulled into unrelated technical education — it burns call time with zero pipeline value.

quote: And the one thing that bugs me about Tesla is Tesla's whole idea was free electricity for everybody
stewart_read: Customer references a prior conversation with another company about a 12-panel system but the rep never probes which company or what was quoted.
coaching_implication: Even on a shade-limited lead, probing the prior quote (company, size, price) builds competitive intel for the floor.
